'''Pierre Gaspard''' (born 6 December 1959)<ref>{{cite web | url=http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n97053997 | title=Gaspard, Pierre | work=Library of Congress | accessdate=27 June 2018}}</ref> is a [[Belgium|Belgian]] physicist and professor at the ''Interdisciplinary Center for Nonlinear Phenomena and Complex Systems'' and the ''Service de Physique Non-Linéaire and Mécanique Statistique'' of the [[Universite Libre de Bruxelles]] (ULB). His research interests are on nonlinear [[physics]], [[statistical physics]], and [[chemical physics]].

Gaspard studied physics at the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]] (ULB) from 1978 to 1982, and completed his doctorate in physics in 1987, directed by {{ill|Grégoire Nicolis|de}}. After postdoctoral studies at the [[University of Chicago]] he became a researcher with the [[National Fund for Scientific Research]] in 1989. He joined ULB as a lecturer in 1996; in 2004 he became a professor and gave up his researcher position.<ref name=acad/>

He won the Théophile De Donder Prize of the [[Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium]] in 1988 and the Adolphe Wetrems Prize in 1995.<ref name=acad/>
In 2006, he was awarded the [[Francqui Prize]] on Exact Sciences for his work on statistical mechanics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.francquifoundation.be/rapport-test/2006-rapport-jury-pierre-gaspard/ |title=2006 &ndash; Rapport Jury Pierre Gaspard |website=[[Francqui Foundation]] |access-date=2018-06-27}}</ref> He has been a member of the [[Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium]] since 2006.<ref name=acad>{{cite web|url=http://www.academieroyale.be/fr/who-who-detail/relations/pierre-gaspard/|title=Pierre Gaspard|publisher=[[Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium]]|accessdate=2018-06-27}}</ref>
